title: Typing an inactive part number in full shows the inactive message
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have an inactive part, part A, with 4 on hand and a hyphen in its part number.
  • Have an active part, part B, with 4 on hand, so the lookup has a part it must still offer.
  • Give parts A and B part numbers that start with the same text, and descriptions that start with the same text, so one search finds both.
  • Create an open work order, work order 1, for this test, with an approved line, line 1, that holds no parts.
  • Start on work order 1, on its Lines tab.
custom_steps:
1. Click Add Part under line 1.
  2. Type part A's part number in lower case in the Part Number field.
  3. Replace the text with part A's part number with spaces in place of its hyphens.
  4. Click the X at the top right of the window.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The New Part Request window opens for line 1 of work order 1, with the Part Number field.

Step 2:

  • The lookup shows part A's part number, written as it was saved (capitals and hyphens), followed by "is inactive. Activate it from the Inactive tab to use it.".
  • No offer to add the number as a special order appears.

Step 3:

  • The same message shows, naming part A as it was saved.
  • No special order is offered.

Step 4:

  • The window closes and line 1 holds no parts.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10822 (Story 9, Inactive Parts Cannot Be Added to New Work)

  • S9-R16: “When the number typed in a part lookup matches an inactive part at this location, the lookup does not offer to add it as a special order. It shows "{part number} is inactive. Activate it from the Inactive tab to use it.", naming the inactive part's number. On technician charge-out, where a typed number is taken straight from the field, the field shows the same message as its error and the line cannot be saved.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Retired number typed in a part lookup | "{part number} is inactive. Activate it from the Inactive tab to use it." | Shown in the lookup in place of the special order offer; on technician charge-out, error under the field”
  • Story 9, context note: “Context note: in S9-R9a, S9-R15, S9-R16 and S9-R17 a number "matches" an inactive part when the two are the same once upper and lower case, hyphens, asterisks, periods and spaces are ignored. A number that also belongs to an active part at this location is not refused.”
  • Key Decisions: “Typing a retired number by hand does not get around it. The lookup does not offer the number as a special order, and the system refuses an inactive part on new work however it arrives (Story 9).”

From: Jira tickets and comments under epic SV-10647 (saved in sources/jira-2026-10-27/ALL-TICKETS-2026-10-27.md), read 27 Oct 2026

  • SV-10822 acceptance criteria: “Given GREASETUBE is inactive, when the user types "greasetube" in full in a part lookup, then no special order is offered and the lookup shows "GREASETUBE is inactive. Activate it from the Inactive tab to use it."”
